en: These creators and these identities that become these real rich relationships that you form.

zh: 这已经成为人们打发时间的基础范式。

zh: 而且往往是这样的：我是想坐着后仰看大屏幕电视，还是就在手机上看几个视频、享受一段美好时光？

speaker: Unknown

en: However, there's things that spin off the short video network that are actually incredible new businesses themselves.

zh: 那是另一个趋势。

en: I mean, the AI vegetable thing is a small part of it, but there are companies like Real Shorts, Drama Fever, Drama Box.
zh: 我是说，AI 蔬菜那类东西只是其中一小部分，但有像 Real Shorts、Drama Fever、Drama Box 这样的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That are creating short stories that are maybe 20, 30, 60 minutes in length, chunked into multiple episodes.

en: And you might on TikTok see, or on Instagram Reels, see the first episode or two, or the first trailer for this wonderful story.
zh: 你可能会在 TikTok 上，或在 Instagram Reels 上，看到第一集或前两集，或者这个精彩故事的第一支预告片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them are like soap operas.
zh: 其中一些就像肥皂剧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them are little fantasy things.
zh: 其中有些是小小的奇幻故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them are mystery and horror, but they kind of get you in.
zh: 有些是悬疑和恐怖,但它们能把你吸引进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead of just kind of, again, flipping one show to the next, that sort of becomes this feed of constant attention switching,
zh: 而不是像之前那样,一个节目接一个节目地翻,这变成了一种不断切换注意力的信息流,

speaker: Unknown
en: This is watching a little bit longer.
zh: 这会让你看得更久一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: This might not quite be a eight hour Netflix series that's costing hundreds of millions to produce, but this is a thing that is cheaper to produce, but it still requires great storytelling.
zh: 这可能还不是那种耗资数亿美元制作的八小时 Netflix 剧集,但这是制作成本更低的东西,却仍然需要出色的讲故事能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And are they mostly AI generated?
zh: 那它们大多是 AI 生成的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, right now these got big even before the AI wave.
zh: 你知道,这些东西甚至在 AI 浪潮之前就已经火起来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of them were actually just filming people and doing things, you know, a little bit on the cheap, but we're creating real shows that made sense or using animation.
zh: 所以很多其实只是拍摄人们做事情,你知道,稍微有点低成本,但做出来的都是讲得通的真实节目,或者用动画。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing a lot more of them now use AI in order to do this and to create these videos.
zh: 我们现在看到越来越多的这类产品使用 AI 来做这件事、来创作这些视频。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like one called Shorticle that I think is primarily AI generated that is, they're great stories.
zh: 有一个叫 Shorticle 的,我认为主要是 AI 生成的,它们的故事很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you go to watch the stories and at least me, I always get hooked and I'm enjoying, you
zh: 就像你去看这些故事,至少对我来说,我总是会上瘾,很享受,

en: You know, just what I'm watching.
zh: 你知道,就是我正在看的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, they're short, they're easily to consume, but you kind of go on the whole narrative arc.
zh: 再说,它们很短,容易消费,但你会走完整个叙事弧线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think with AI, we're democratizing creation of these so much that we're going to see massive new platforms for storytellers, not just for a short video that's a little bit gimmicky, but a real story.
zh: 我认为借助 AI,我们正在极大地民主化这类内容的创作,我们将看到为讲故事的人打造的大型新平台,不只是那种有点噱头性质的短视频,而是真正的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we'll still have our TikToks.
zh: 所以我们还是会有我们的 TikTok。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you just want to watch something that's kind of in your zone and in your area and just be able to watch it on your phone and just flip through it, these micro drama platforms, I think are going to become so much bigger.
zh: 但当你只想看点符合你自己圈子和领域的东西,并且能在手机上直接看、随手翻看时,我认为这些微短剧平台会变得大得多。

zh: 能够做一个独立的应用才算得上值得风投投资吗?

zh: 还是你认为工作室模式也行,比如它们就在 TikTok 上,可以吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So most of these already are standalone apps, because what you'll do is on TikTok, you'll see the beginning of the show or a trailer for it.
zh: 大多数其实已经是独立应用了,因为你在 TikTok 上会看到节目的开头或预告片。

zh: 我是说,已经有数十亿美元流进这个品类了。

zh: 但我认为借助 AI,我们能够提升讲故事的水平,提升创造力,打造让任何有故事想讲的人都能把它放进这些平台的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just like TikTok, let anybody be a creator of a short video.
zh: 就像 TikTok 让任何人都能成为短视频创作者一样。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 这将让任何会讲故事的人都能把作品发出去,获得越来越大的受众。

en: Are you optimistic about AI-generated feature films?
zh: 你对 AI 生成的长片电影乐观吗?

zh: 较短的内容,你可以更多地测试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see, oh, are people responding to it, lean into it, build the next segment.
zh: 你可以看到,哦,人们是否有反应,然后顺势加码,做下一段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think we'll have movies that are AI-generated?
zh: 你认为我们会有 AI 生成的电影吗?

zh: 我是说,长期答案当然是会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I tend to think we always try to jump to the end game.
zh: 我倾向于认为我们总是想直接跳到终局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's beautiful about startups and the startup ecosystem and the venture ecosystem is that we don't always need to boil the ocean on day one.
zh: 而创业公司和创业生态以及风投生态的美妙之处在于,我们不需要在第一天就煮干整个海洋。

speaker: Unknown
en: We build something that meets today and that can deliver a great experience today, but it may not be the biggest thing.
zh: 我们做的是满足当下、能在今天提供出色体验的东西,但它可能不是最大的那件事。

en: I remember the early days of YouTube, one of the best quotes that was told to me was, we're not, you know, it was like, how are you ever going to compete with like network TV?
zh: 我记得 YouTube 早期,别人跟我说过的最好的话之一是,我们不是,你知道,当时像是,你怎么可能和网络电视竞争?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而回答是,我们的目标不是打败网络电视最精彩的那一小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, you know, if you still want to watch an incredible, you know, I think Grey's Anatomy was a really popular show at the time, Grey's Anatomy, you should still watch Grey's Anatomy.
zh: 事实上,你知道,如果你还是想看非常精彩的节目,我记得当时《实习医生格蕾》是真的很火的剧,《实习医生格蕾》,那你还是应该去看《实习医生格蕾》。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're trying to beat the worst hour of TV.
zh: 但我们想打败的是电视最糟糕的那一小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because if we're more interesting to find things on YouTube than your worst hour of TV...
zh: 因为如果我们在 YouTube 上找到有趣的东西比你电视最糟的一小时更有意思……

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll start to spend that hour on YouTube instead of on TV.
zh: 你就会开始把那一小时花在 YouTube 上而不是电视上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's very much true.
zh: 所以我认为这个道理非常成立。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, you don't need to beat Netflix and Hulu today, but you need to beat the, I don't really know what to watch.
zh: 再说,你今天不需要打败 Netflix 和 Hulu,但你需要打败那个「我真不知道该看什么」的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm just kind of surfing around.
zh: 我就随便翻翻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish I had a little bit better story.
zh: 真希望有个稍微好一点的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Be that better story.
zh: 成为那个更好的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you start to fill from the bottom.
zh: 现在你开始从底部往上填。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as you build new franchises, you build stories, as you build characters, it can move all the way up.
zh: 然后随着你打造新的系列、打造故事、打造角色，它可以一路往上延伸。

zh: 在我看来，我会把它们归类为这样一类东西：它们试图在某种生态系统中积蓄能量并强行实现它，人们……你知道，有些人怀疑 Instinct 有 Clubhouse 的味道，你知道，风投们对它非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're obviously, you know,
zh: 它们显然，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: What, like Foursquare and Twitter launched itself by this sort of had this sort of insider community is going to willing to be in it.
zh: 什么，就像 Foursquare 和 Twitter 通过这种拥有内部人社区的方式推出，愿意参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your reflection?
zh: 你的反思是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, will there be another like the venture community, the Silicon Valley community of insiders sort of gets excited and that catapults it or is that past or what's your reflection on that?
zh: 比如说，会不会再有 venture 圈子、硅谷内部人圈子变得兴奋并将其推上高潮的情况，还是那种时代已经过去了？你对这有什么反思？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think there's two different things, because I think with things like Meerkat that was so tied to Twitter and Clubhouse, that definitely started from a vibe of people who were very much in the tech and Twitter ecosystems and able to grow.
zh: 我是说，我觉得这是两件不同的事，因为我觉得像 Meerkat 这种和 Twitter 绑定得如此紧密的东西，还有 Clubhouse，确实是从一个主要由身处科技和 Twitter 生态、并且有能力实现增长的人所形成的氛围中起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were all about bringing people together live.
zh: 而它们都是关于把人们实时地聚到一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what both of these companies showed is how magical that moment is, how magical that experience is when we're having live, but also how hard it is to scale when you're only live.
zh: 我觉得这两家公司都展示了那一刻有多神奇，当我们实时互动时那种体验有多神奇，但同时也展示了当你只有实时时，扩张有多难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the products we've talked about TikTok and Instagram and everything else are very much async.
zh: 我们谈到过的大多数产品，TikTok 和 Instagram 以及其他一切，都非常地异步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so how do you combine a product that is async and live to be a large platform?
zh: 那么你如何把一个异步产品和实时结合成一个大平台？

speaker: Unknown
en: What has turned out is that the platforms that are large and async can add live components and have those work rather than a fully live network becoming the next big thing.
zh: 结果证明，那些已经很大且异步的平台可以添加实时组件并让它们奏效，而不是一个完全实时的网络成为下一个大事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's always been the challenge with some of those companies.
zh: 而且我觉得这一直是那其中一些公司的挑战。

en: To separate your other part of your question, I sense you're talking about kind of the Silicon Valley energy of technology and technologists discovering something new and bringing that to the world.
zh: 把你问题的另一部分拆开来说，我感觉到你说的是那种科技和科技人的硅谷能量——发现新东西并把它带给世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually think the magic's back.
zh: 而且我实际上觉得那种魔力回来了。

en: I think with AI, the beginning people who really understood AI were the tinkerers, were the ones who would not just get ChatGPT and be like, I can type in what I type into Google, ooh, that's a little bit better result, but I can type in really complex incantations and start to get really thoughtful, different responses.
zh: 我认为在 AI 的早期，真正理解 AI 的人是那些折腾者，是那些不只是拿到 ChatGPT 然后说“我可以把我输入 Google 的东西输进去，哦，结果好一点点”，而是能输入非常复杂的咒语并开始得到非常有思考深度的、不同回应的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Remember all those prompts that were shared in the early days of people with ChatGPT?
zh: 还记得 ChatGPT 早期人们分享的那些提示词吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine that you're a detective and you're trying to solve this problem.
zh: 想象你是一个侦探，你正试图解决这个案子。

en: Well, here's all the evidence I have.
zh: 好的，这是我掌握的全部证据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you please help me figure out what's going on or what are the three steps that I should do next?
zh: 你能帮我弄清楚发生了什么，或者我接下来应该做哪三步吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: With Google, if you ever type that into Google, it would throw up before they really added their AI mode.
zh: 用 Google，如果你把这种内容输进 Google，在他们真正加入 AI 模式之前，它会被顶得吃不消。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with ChatGPT...
zh: 而用 ChatGPT……

speaker: Unknown
en: It would give you a great answer and the more and more complex prompts.
zh: 它会给你一个很好的答案，提示词越复杂越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as technologies were figuring that out and then they were figuring out what they could build on top of these APIs, things like OpenClaw were very much a tech phenomenon.
zh: 而随着那些人搞明白这一点，然后搞清楚他们能在这些 API 之上构建什么，像 OpenClaw 这样的东西在很大程度上是一种科技现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're discovering things again that reminds me of the very earliest days of the tech ecosystem where technologists, builders, tinkerers get this first.
zh: 我们又在重新发现一些东西，这让我想起科技生态最早的那些日子，那时科技人、建造者、折腾者最先得到这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now we're at this incredible wave.
zh: 而现在我们正处于这波不可思议的浪潮中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of why I came back to VC is turning from that moment to how do we consumerize this?
zh: 我回到 VC 的部分原因，就是从那一刻转向：我们如何把这变成消费级的？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we truly make it available to most people?
zh: 我们如何真正让它对大多数人可用？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I look at Instinct as one of the coolest phenomenons of a startup that is like taking a bunch of this complex technology.
zh: 而我把 Instinct 看作一个初创公司最酷的现象之一，它就像是在把一大堆这种复杂技术……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's one of the first that really was like, how do I make it super easy?
zh: 它是最早真正在问“我如何让它变得超级简单？”的其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give Polk some credit.
zh: 我得给 Polk 一些肯定。

speaker: Unknown
en: They discovered, you know, putting this just through texting, through iMessage made their, you know, it made it so much easier to interact even than going to a complex website and other things.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're at this great wave where sure it gets exciting in the tech community, but that's because we've already been tinkering for so long.
zh: 所以我们正处于这波伟大的浪潮中，当然它在科技圈里令人兴奋，但那是因为我们已经折腾了很久了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The rest of the world hasn't been on that journey in the same way.
zh: 而世界上其他人还没有以同样的方式走过那段旅程。

en: You know, many of them are very heavy users of AI now, ChatGPT, other things.
zh: 你知道，他们中许多人现在已经是 AI 的重度用户了，ChatGPT，还有其他东西。

en: There's also a lot of resistance to AI because we're telling such bad narratives about how this could replace all jobs or kill everybody as opposed to enable the next incredible wave of innovation, which I very much believe in.
zh: 对 AI 也有很大的抵触，因为我们讲述的叙事如此糟糕——说它会取代所有工作或者杀死所有人——而不是说它会开启下一波不可思议的创新浪潮，而这一点我深信不疑。

en: Well, yeah, one of the reasons I'm excited you're back is, to me, in Silicon Valley, you represented, like, you were very optimistic.
zh: 嗯，是啊，我为你回来感到兴奋的原因之一是，在我看来，在硅谷，你代表着，比如，你非常乐观。

zh: 是否有过某种冲动，想把 AI 变成一个动词之类的？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 你知道，我认为操作系统里一个非常酷的东西显然是 Siri 和助手，它是其中非常重要的一部分，但你每天做的很多其他事情，AI 都可以帮上忙。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, some of that is sometimes you get 30 notifications and they stack up and actually having a summary that gives you a little bit of a lens and what's in there before you tap and expand can be helpful.
zh: 你知道，其中一些是，有时候你会收到 30 条通知，它们堆积起来，实际上有一个摘要，在你点击展开之前给你一个了解里面内容的小窗口，会很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, text, it has to be like 200 characters or more or something before they actually get summarized.
zh: 你知道，文本，必须达到 200 个字符或更多之类的，才会真正被摘要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if someone sends you a diatribe, it's sometimes nice to get the quick glance and you can always again tap to expand it.
zh: 如果有人给你发了一篇长篇大论，有时候快速浏览一下是挺好的，而且你总是可以再点击展开它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think what Apple did really well with Apple intelligence was not just was focused on the assistant, which took longer than it needed to, but
zh: 所以我认为 Apple 在 Apple Intelligence 上做得非常好的地方在于，不仅仅是专注于助手，虽然那花的时间比必要的要长，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: Also focus on a supporting cast of other features around the operating system that are just better with AI, whether that's writing tools right in the moment to help you rewrite things, whether that's in the photos app, being able to, you know, edit your photos or clean them up or, you know, expand them now, which just got launched, or this really cool feature around spatial reframing where you can actually tilt the camera a little bit because it has a lot of spatial knowledge.
zh: 也专注于围绕操作系统的其他一组辅助功能，它们有了 AI 会变得更好，无论是当下就能帮你改写内容的写作工具，还是照片应用里能够，你知道的，编辑你的照片或清理它们，或者，你知道的，现在刚上线的扩展照片功能，还有这个围绕空间重构的非常酷的功能，你可以真正地稍微倾斜相机，因为它拥有大量的空间知识。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can sort of fill in any gaps even after you took the photo.
zh: 它甚至可以在你拍完照片之后填补任何空缺。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've used it to like, I left a sign sticking out of my daughter's head and was able to
zh: 我用过它，比如，我拍了一张招牌从我女儿头上伸出来的照片，然后能够

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, move it around so it didn't look as funny because it was otherwise a great picture of her.
zh: 你知道的，把它移开，这样看起来就没那么滑稽了，因为那本来是她的一张很棒的照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's so many other things that you want, but it's not AI for the sake of AI.
zh: 所以还有很多其他你想要的东西，但这不是为了 AI 而 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's AI for the sake of features you always wanted to build that makes life easier and that think, hopefully, now that there are these LLM tools, we can actually power them.
zh: 这是为了那些你一直想构建的、能让生活更轻松的功能而用 AI，而且我想，希望现在有了这些 LLM 工具，我们能够真正为它们提供动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've left the device company in the world.
zh: 所以你离开了世界上那家设备公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they're clearly open AIs working on devices.
zh: 你知道，他们显然 OpenAI 正在做设备。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're startups.
zh: 我想还有创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who are thinking about it.
zh: 正在思考这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you optimistic?
zh: 你乐观吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess if I say optimistic, you're going to say yes.
zh: 我想如果我说乐观，你会说是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: What device category?
zh: 什么设备类别？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think we will have new sort of AI devices or do you think existing devices will become imbued with AI powers?
zh: 你认为我们会有新的人工智能设备，还是你认为现有设备会被赋予 AI 能力？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do we yearn for a pen or ear pods, whatever we're calling them that are AI native or people have talked about?
zh: 我们会渴望一支笔或耳机，不管我们怎么称呼它们，它们是 AI 原生的，或者人们谈论过的？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, sort of a portable disk.
zh: 你知道的，某种便携式磁盘。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have a view on what types of devices lend themselves to AI?
zh: 你对什么类型的设备适合 AI 有看法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think we are at the dawn of what's hopefully an incredible explosion of new AI capabilities that are going to make a lot of these devices a lot more useful.
zh: 你知道，我认为我们正处于一场希望是令人难以置信的 AI 新能力爆发的黎明，它将使很多这样的设备有用得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, what is really powerful with AI?
zh: 你知道，AI 真正强大的地方是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: When it senses data and it can get more information in, and then when it can use that to help compute things and deliver them back to you in a useful way and take action for you.
zh: 当它感知数据并能获取更多信息时，然后当它能够利用这些信息帮助你计算事物，并以有用的方式把它们交付给你，并替你采取行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of what we're seeing are things that look like more sensors, whether there's always on recording, even the new Apple Watch can do some of that.
zh: 所以我们看到的很多东西看起来像更多的传感器，无论是始终开启的录音，甚至新的 Apple Watch 也能做到其中一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know, I was shocked by that, that they're going to let you sort of just record ambiently.
zh: 我知道，我对此感到震惊，他们要让你可以某种程度地进行环境录音。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's very much in a privacy safe, very moderated way, but I think that's an incredible feature, but there'll be other devices that will help us do that.
zh: 我认为这在很大程度上是一种隐私安全、非常受控的方式，但我认为那是一个难以置信的功能，而且会有其他设备帮助我们做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll be certainly other things that can be on the lookout for us, whether that's eventually coming into smart glasses or things in our ears or things we'll wear on our shirts.
zh: 肯定会有其他东西能够为我们留意周围，无论是最终进入智能眼镜，还是我们耳朵里的东西，或者我们戴在衬衫上的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure which things will catch.
zh: 我不确定哪些东西会流行起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm less the perfect creator, but I think the people who are designing these things and building them that have visions, like we can very much, you know, and Dracen Horst helped them amplify those.
zh: 我不太算是完美的创造者，但我认为那些设计这些东西并构建它们的人有愿景，就像我们可以，你知道的，Dracen Horst 帮助他们放大这些愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a moment for new hardware just as much as new software.
zh: 这是新硬件的时刻，和新软件一样重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, again, the inputs, you know, it's still work to like pull your phone out of your pocket to say something and have it do something.
zh: 你知道的，再说一次，输入方面，你知道的，从口袋里掏出手机说点什么并让它做点什么，仍然是件麻烦事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, when you're wearing your AirPods and you have Siri there, you can just quickly ask questions or get things out that you don't have to initially pull something out of your pocket.
zh: 你知道的，当你戴着 AirPods 并且 Siri 在那里时，你可以快速提问或者获取东西，而不必一开始就从口袋里掏出什么东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the dream of the glasses and you can capture things and remember them.
zh: 这就是眼镜的梦想，你可以捕捉事物并记住它们。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 如果我们戴眼镜的话，我很乐意拥有智能眼镜。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, why not?
zh: 就像是，为什么不呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I focus on buying the most, like,
zh: 我是说，我专注于购买最，像，

speaker: Unknown
en: Unbreakable and lightest glass as possible.
zh: 不易碎和尽可能轻的眼镜。

speaker: Unknown
en: I break glasses at the hinge a lot, so these actually have a hinge that I can reset.
zh: 我经常把眼镜在铰链处弄坏，所以这些眼镜实际上有一个我可以重置的铰链。

speaker: Unknown
en: On one hand, once it's as light and easy as my glasses, I would love it if they were AI-powered.
zh: 一方面，一旦它像我的眼镜一样轻便易用，如果它们是 AI 驱动的，我会很喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: My daughter is 11 months and she rips off my glasses all the time, so that's the new problem.
zh: 我女儿 11 个月大，她总是扯掉我的眼镜，所以这是新问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we about to enter a world where-
zh: 我们是否即将进入一个世界，其中——

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything is recorded.
zh: 一切都被记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a transcript of everything.
zh: 我们拥有 everything 的转录文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: In some way, I'm not so opposed, but there are a lot of problems with that, certainly in a business culture.
zh: 从某种程度上说，我并不那么反对，但这其中确实存在很多问题，尤其是在商业文化中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you optimistic that we're just going to ambiently record everything so that all these companies have the data they want to give us all this value?
zh: 你是否乐观地认为，我们将会自然而然地记录一切，这样所有这些公司就拥有了它们想要的数据，从而给我们提供所有这些价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think we are definitely in a world of building new norms.
zh: 你知道，我认为我们确实处于一个建立新规范的世界中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think, you know, on video calls, it's very easy for people to have both a recorder that's visible to other people and even one that is not.
zh: 而且我认为，你知道，在视频通话中，人们很容易既拥有一个其他人可见的录制器，甚至拥有一个不可见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the world, we still haven't figured out the norms yet of when this is there.
zh: 在这个世界上，我们还没有搞清楚它存在时的规范。

speaker: Unknown
en: If something were to have a camera that could take pictures, being able to trust what the person is actually doing, where they're using it, and what our new norms are, like this is not something that's going to like be solved overnight.
zh: 如果某个东西带有一个可以拍照的摄像头，能够信任这个人实际在做什么、他们在哪里使用它，以及我们的新规范是什么——这不是能一夜之间解决的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think a world where we have these additive things to help us remember things and keep track of things and hold ourselves accountable to what we said we were going to do and recall cool things we heard about is a really, really useful pattern.
zh: 但我确实认为，一个拥有这些附加工具来帮助我们记住事情、跟踪事情、让我们对自己说过要做的事情负责、并回想起我们听到过的很酷的事情的世界，是一个非常非常有用的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the right to forget and the right to not remember and not record and have safe spaces is really valuable too.
zh: 而遗忘的权利、不去记住和不去记录的权利、拥有安全空间，也同样非常有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's so much trust that goes all, you know, all of it.
zh: 但这其中需要大量的信任，贯穿其中的所有环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the moment you tell someone a secret, the secret is no longer yours, but you have trust in that person.
zh: 我是说，当你告诉别人一个秘密的那一刻，这个秘密就不再只属于你了，但你信任那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're going to have to figure out with whatever tools and with whatever people, that same level of trust and safety continues to be there.
zh: 所以我们将不得不搞清楚，无论用什么工具、和什么人，同样的信任和安全水平能持续存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to have much more meetings with like no devices because there's so much ambient recording going on.
zh: 我们将会有更多不带设备的会议，因为环境录音实在是太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: No device meetings in the sound room.
zh: 在隔音房间里开无设备会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or if any one of us is recording this, share it with everybody and trust that it's still Chatham House rules or whatever set of rules.
zh: 或者，如果我们中有任何一个人在录音，就分享给所有人，并相信它仍然遵循查塔姆守则或 whatever 的某套规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I have chat groups with people that sure, everything's recorded in the chat group, but everybody trusts each other.
zh: 我有一些和别人的聊天群，当然，聊天群里的一切都被记录着，但大家彼此信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there is always some risk that one person could burn the chat group.
zh: 当然总是存在某个人可能毁掉这个聊天群的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you just have deep trust and deep vetting, you know, and that's why is that, you know, on chat that different than in person, but these are all norms and trust that have to get built out.
zh: 你就是要有深度的信任和深度的审查，你知道，这就是为什么在聊天软件上和面对面有什么不同呢，但这些全都是必须建立起来的规范和信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of it's not software, it's humans.
zh: 而且其中很多不是软件的事，是人的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, the decision to go to Andreessen Horowitz and I mean, both to get, there's one decision, get back into venture.
zh: 我很好奇，你去 Andreessen Horowitz 的决定，我是说，这里面有两个决定，一是重新回到风险投资行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd like to hear about that.
zh: 我想听听关于这个的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then how did you pick the venture firm you did?
zh: 然后你是怎么挑选你选的那家风投公司的？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, as we talked about this moment last fall of seeing OpenClaw.
zh: 你知道，正如我们谈到去年秋天看到 OpenClaw 的那个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Reminded me for the first time that you can build consumer startups again where the models are a piece of the puzzle but are not the actual value.
zh: 它第一次让我想起，你可以重新做消费级创业公司了，模型只是拼图中的一块，而不是实际的价值所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the value is really in the software that's created around it.
zh: 而价值真正在于围绕它创建的软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before that, while I was working at Apple, I really wanted to make sure that we got Siri back and shipped.
zh: 在那之前，当我在 Apple 工作的时候，我真的想确保我们把 Siri 挽救回来并发布出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also had the belief that to build a great startup right now, you actually need model innovation.
zh: 我当时也有一个信念，那就是要在现在打造一家伟大的创业公司，你实际上需要模型创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't have researchers on staff, you aren't building a startup that is truly differentiated.
zh: 而如果你没有研究人员在团队里，你打造就不是一家真正有差异化的创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But once I saw OpenClaw and then all the things we've seen built since, and even what we were building with Siri, Apple did a great partnership with Google to use some of Google's frontier models, but it still is so much software built into Siri that is way more complex than the model itself, reminded me, you can build consumer startups again.
zh: 但一旦我看到 OpenClaw，以及之后我们看到的所有被构建出来的东西，甚至我们用 Siri 在构建的东西——Apple 与 Google 达成了一次很棒的合作，使用 Google 的一些前沿模型，但 Siri 里仍然内置了如此多的软件，比模型本身复杂得多——这提醒了我，你可以重新做消费级创业公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that got me like,
zh: 所以这让我，

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, as I spend, you know, my 50s, you know, I'd really rather be helping companies and I really want to help the startup ecosystem again.
zh: 你知道，在我度过我 50 多岁的这段时间，你知道，我真的更愿意去帮助公司，我真的很想再次帮助创业生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I believe it's possible.
zh: 而且我相信这是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when I thought about that, you know, I had an incredible experience at Greylock.
zh: 然后当我想到这一点时，你知道，我在 Greylock 有一段非常棒的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a great set of partners.
zh: 多么出色的一群合伙人啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they've decided they're not as focused right now on consumer and, you know, maybe they'll get back into that again.
zh: 你知道，他们已经决定现在不再那么专注于消费领域了，你知道，也许他们以后会重新回到那个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as I talked to them, that was not their focus.
zh: 但在我和他们交谈时，那确实不是他们的重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I thought of all the firms that I've gotten to know over the years and seen.
zh: 于是我想起了这些年来我认识并见过的所有公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which one did I see really stand by founders always and was really built with a whole different way of supporting founders and of all the bad things I've seen in venture?
zh: 我看到哪一家始终真正坚定地站在创始人一边，并且真正是以一种完全不同的支持创始人的方式建立的，而在我见过的风险投资行业的所有糟糕的事情中？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of stuff that ends up becoming anti-founder that never gets talked about in the world.
zh: 有很多东西最终变成了反创始人的，却从未被世人谈论过。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the firm that I felt really had never crossed those lines?
zh: 哪一家公司让我觉得从来没有越过那些底线？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was Andreessen Horowitz.
zh: 那就是 Andreessen Horowitz。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I knew a couple of the folks there and was fortunate enough to kind of pitch them something that I wanted to do and be part of the venture ecosystem and ended up becoming a great match.
zh: 所以我认识了那里的几个人，而且有幸向他们推介了一些我想做的事情，成为风险投资生态系统的一部分，最终证明是非常好的匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: So are you like investing or there's another layer to that?
zh: 那么，你是在做投资，还是其中还有另一层？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I'm doing a combination of supporting investments and helping companies and, you know, I'll be helping us do new deals, but it's unclear.
zh: 你知道，我在做的是支持投资项目和帮助公司的组合，你知道，我也会帮助我们做新的交易，但这还不明确。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not necessarily going to lead a whole bunch of deals myself.
zh: 我不一定会亲自主导一大堆交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you want to sort of like give product advice?
zh: 比如说你想提供一些产品建议之类的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, really give product strategy, growth advice, and really be part of the team that's helping to support companies.
zh: 是的，主要是提供产品战略、增长建议，并且真正成为帮助支持公司的团队中的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really what Andreessen does is it's not just you get one person who you can call sometimes, but you get actually a team of support.
zh: 这正是 Andreessen 的做法：不只是你能时不时打电话给一个人，而是你实际上得到一个支持团队。

en: And so I'm meeting a ton of founders, new founders.
zh: 所以我正在见大量的创始人，新创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like to say future founders and existing founders in the portfolio and helping them be great.
zh: 我喜欢说，是未来的创始人和投资组合中的现有创始人，并帮助他们变得伟大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I find new founders, I'll partner with them on getting new investments done with Andreessen Horowitz and we'll get to go build great companies.
zh: 而当我发现新的创始人时,我会与他们合作,通过 Andreessen Horowitz 完成新的投资,我们将一起打造伟大的公司。

en: What is sort of the growth playbook at the moment?

en: I mean, how do you...

en: I mean, I care about this in my own business.

en: It's like, oh, for a while, email was a core one.

en: It's so hard to get customers and attention.

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Andreessen Horowitz has succeeded in sort of the launch.
zh: 我是说,Andreessen Horowitz 在发布这一块上算是成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I feel like you guys deliver like launch in a box.
zh: 就是,我感觉你们提供的好像是「一站式发布」。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's some, you know, pushback that...
zh: 我认为存在一些,你知道,反对意见……

speaker: Unknown
en: All right, that playbook has been done.
zh: 好吧,那套打法已经被用过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, it only sustains if you keep coming up with like, what's the new one that's differentiated?
zh: 而且就是,只有你不断想出新的、有差异化的东西,它才能持续下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, right, you've got the launch video, that's now table stakes, what's the next thing?
zh: 就是说,对吧,你有了发布视频,那现在是基本门槛了,下一个是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's always an arms race, no matter like how good you get.
zh: 所以永远存在军备竞赛,不管你做得多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't know if you were talking to...
zh: 但我不知道你是不是在和……

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, like a consumer seed startup that's like, I need to get 1,000 people on this app.
zh: 是的,比如一个消费级种子期初创公司,像是我需要让 1000 个人用上这个应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a platform you're bullish on or what's your advice?
zh: 有没有你看好的平台,或者你的建议是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great question if you ask this.
zh: 如果你问这个问题,这是个很好的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's one of the things that it's not yet clear that there's some new growth distribution vector in AI.
zh: 而且这也是其中一件事:目前还不清楚 AI 领域是否存在某种新的增长分发渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: There really are the channels we all use to communicate and spend attention on.
zh: 真正存在的还是我们所有人用来交流、投入注意力的那些渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I always tell people the first most important thing is have a great product.
zh: 但我总是告诉人们,第一件最重要的事是拥有一个出色的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have a product that people
zh: 拥有一个人们

speaker: Unknown
en: Love, use, come back to, find a place in their life and use regularly.
zh: 喜爱、使用、会回访、在生活中找到位置并定期使用的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, for somebody like you who's doing a newsletter and a set of events, it's have a community that is like, I want to read what Eric is going to say next.
zh: 补充说明一下:我经常谈到的一个问题是,用户在你的产品里做什么动作?

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time I read what Eric has to say, it's smart, it enriches my life so that I want to keep coming back.
zh: 每次我读 Eric 说的话,都很聪明,丰富了我的生活,所以我想一直回来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a product that you use, it has to have that same experience.
zh: 对于一个你使用的产品,它必须有同样的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am glad I used the product for this purpose.
zh: 我很高兴我为这个目的使用了这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I want to keep doing it.
zh: 而且我想继续用下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talk a lot about what is the action someone's doing in your product?
zh: 我经常谈论一个问题：用户在你的产品里做的动作到底是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the purpose of why they're coming to your product?
zh: 他们来用你的产品的目的是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the cycle at which you expect them to use your product?
zh: 你期望他们以什么样的周期来使用你的产品?

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to deeply understand that.
zh: 你需要深入理解这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And without that, growth doesn't matter at all.
zh: 没有这个,增长根本不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But once you have that, then it's finding ways to tell your story.
zh: 但一旦你有了这个,接下来就是找到讲述你故事的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's different channels that depend on the product and who you're trying to reach.
zh: 而渠道有很多种,取决于产品以及你想触达的人群。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're trying to reach people in the tech community and the tinkerers and everything else, Twitter's an amazing platform to have conversation.
zh: 如果你想触达科技圈的人、喜欢折腾的人等等,Twitter 是一个进行对话的绝佳平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very obvious that as you have good conversations there, they can spread and they can grow.
zh: 而且很明显,当你在那里有好的对话时,它们可以传播、可以增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're trying to target teens, you need to be using the platforms that they're on and speak to them in a way that is meaningful to them, whether that's more on Instagram or on TikTok.
zh: 如果你想瞄准青少年,你需要使用他们所在平台,并用对他们有意义的方式与他们交流,无论是在 Instagram 还是在 TikTok 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've seen incredible growth that comes from engaging with creators who tell stories themselves about the products that they use.
zh: 而且我们见过令人难以置信的增长,来自于与创作者合作,由他们自己讲述他们所使用产品的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the creators are getting really, really savvy.
zh: 而且这些创作者现在变得非常、非常精明。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, sometimes they are paid, but even then, they only advocate for things that they believe in.
zh: 现在,有时他们是有偿的,但即便如此,他们也只会为自己真正相信的东西代言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some of the best strategies I've heard are, if you want to go talk about something that's health and fitness, don't necessarily go to the health and fitness gurus.
zh: 而我听过的一些最好的策略是,如果你想推广健康和健身类的东西,不一定要去找那些健康和健身达人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to the people who are telling stories about their daily lives, the moms, the young girls or whatever, and introduce the health product to them.
zh: 去找那些讲述自己日常生活故事的人,比如妈妈们、年轻女孩之类的,把健康产品介绍给她们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they'll talk about how it enhances their life.
zh: 然后她们会谈到这如何改善了她们的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now the people who follow them and are interested in them hear their regular stories of their day and the new products they're using too.
zh: 这样,关注她们、对她们感兴趣的人就会听到她们日常生活的故事,以及她们正在使用的新产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: As opposed to the health and fitness guru that just keeps pitching another health and fitness product every single week.
zh: 而不是那种每个星期都在推销另一种健康和健身产品的健身达人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are so many different ways to take your story and the product and find ways to get it in the right hands of your users, but you fundamentally have to know what the, it has to deliver on that or the loop won't work at all.
zh: 所以有很多不同的方式可以把你的故事和产品送到合适的用户手中,但你从根本上必须知道,产品必须在这一点上兑现,否则整个循环根本不会起作用。
